absent: Locking discipline for alternative patching, GIC access, timer descriptors and ACPI state is not shown.
Full boot sequencing for ACPI parsing, CPU bring-up and NUMA formation beyond the constant predicates shown.
Complete layout and semantics of MADT, FADT and firmware memory-attribute tables beyond the cited fields.
PMU event encodings, counter widths and interrupt routing beyond enable, mode and overflow summaries.
GIC priority values, distributor programming and ITS command formatting beyond the register helpers.
Timer erratum matching logic, clock-event programming effects and vDSO interaction beyond the descriptor shape.

findings.text: Enabling and disabling of ACPI globally is exposed through small helpers that set three related disabled indicators together, while processor identity helpers map a logical index to hardware identity and report that every processor appears in the MADT. Package fixup and early CPU initialization are defined as having no effect on this architecture.

The preferred CPU bring-up method is selected by first testing for PSCI compliance derived from boot flags, then testing a parking protocol predicate that is currently defined as never valid, otherwise reporting no method. Mailbox installation for the parking protocol is defined as a no-effect operation.

Memory protections for ACPI mappings are chosen from firmware memory attributes with a fixed precedence that prefers write-back, then write-combining, then write-through, otherwise device semantics. Write-through handling emits a one-time notice and substitutes non-cacheable normal memory rather than allocating a dedicated cacheability encoding.

Capability availability is queried through helpers that first discard build-impossible capabilities and then test either a runtime patch site or a system-wide bitset. One query reports priority-masking use, another reports whether a given numeric capability is present on all processors, and a third maps many named capabilities to build options with a default of available.

CPU-interface access is provided by small helpers that each perform one system-register read or write for a distinct encoding, with an instruction barrier after the writes issued by the DIR, CTLR, IGRPEN1 and SRE helpers and a data barrier after the common IAR read. Two generic helpers form a system encoding from a supplied register token for reads and writes.

Redistributor and ITS tables are accessed with relaxed loads and stores for type, router and table-base state, including virtualization counterparts and command-queue pointers. A helper converts an address range into a point-of-coherency clean-and-invalidate operation.

Mask control provides an operation to write a designated mask constant and, when priority masking is in use, to write it and then execute a DAIF-clear write for PNMIs. A separate predicate reports whether relaxed synchronization for the mask is available based on a system capability.

Physical and virtual counter values are read with an alternative that selects between two system encodings under capability control. Stable reads are routed through an erratum indirection and then through an ordering-enforcement sequence, while frequency and kernel-control registers expose direct read and barrier-guarded write access.

Timer control and compare values for physical and virtual views are written and partially read through dispatch on access kind and register selector. Unsupported selectors are treated as build-time errors, and control writes are followed by an ordering barrier.

Erratum handling for unstable counters has two build variants: one consults a per-processor workaround descriptor and reports presence or selects either the override or the default timer operation, with an ordering barrier before using an override; the other is a constant variant that always reports absence and always selects the default operation.

Patch descriptors record signed offsets from the descriptor to the original sequence and to its replacement, a numeric capability selecting when the replacement applies, and two small lengths for original and replacement extents with the replacement constrained not to exceed the original. A callback type is defined as a function pointer taking at least a descriptor pointer.

Timer errata are described by a match discriminator with DT, local-capability and ACPI OEM variants, an opaque identifier, a description string, optional overrides for two counter reads and two event programming operations, and a flag requesting compat vDSO suppression.

A MADT interrupt-controller entry is considered malformed when it is null, shorter than the offset of a trailing efficiency field, or extends beyond a supplied table end. Length thresholds for optional extensions are defined as the offset of the extension field plus the size of a 16-bit field.

Four context-loss indicators are assigned successive low bit positions for core, trace and two interrupt-controller components. The architected idle-flag translation maps core context loss to a timer-stop request and maps all other combinations to no flags.

Alternative code sites emit an original sequence plus a separate section entry plus an alternate sequence, with entries carrying label distance, replacement distance, capability identifier and both lengths. A high bit marks callback-based entries, build gating can suppress emission entirely, and a shorthand selects a default enabled configuration.

Physical processor identifiers are 64-bit with a designated invalid value, strict specification compliance is required with no out-of-spec workarounds, OS I/O remap is aliased to a same-named implementation, and several NUMA and error-handling helpers are defined as constant failures or no-ops. Table upgrade memory is bounded by the accessible allocation limit.

Ordering primitives provide instruction synchronization, data synchronization with a selectable option, a parameterized no-op filler, and a counter ordering enforcement that derives a stack address through a counter-dependent sequence and performs a discarded load.
Each examined header defines a uniquely named preprocessor macro for inclusion protection.

Apple performance counters zero through nine are exposed as implementation-defined system encodings sharing common leading fields, using selectors zero through seven for the first eight counters and nine and ten for the last two.

Apple performance control, event-select and status encodings provide enable and interrupt-mode fields, per-counter exception-level counting controls, event selectors for a subset of counters, and a ten-bit overflow summary.
The callback discriminator occupies bit fifteen and a CMC disable flag is fixed to one.

Module-time alternative patching is defined in the examined configuration as an immediate success without scanning, while SEA claiming and NUMA initialization each report a fixed negative error and related NUMA and parking helpers are no-ops or constant answers.

A ThunderX-specific IAR sequence inserts fixed no-op delays and an external barrier between AP1R0 and IAR reads and validates progress by comparing two successive AP1R0 reads, substituting a fixed constant when no progress is observed. Counter reads include explicit ordering enforcement, and write-through firmware memory avoids allocating a dedicated MAIR entry.

Interrupt acknowledge operates in two modes selected by an erratum capability gate: a common mode and a ThunderX mode that adds delay, barrier and validation handling before choosing between the observed IAR value and a fixed constant.

Stable counter acquisition is modeled as erratum-aware selection followed by a capability-gated hardware read followed by ordering enforcement, with the hardware read choosing between two encodings under capability control.
External build-time failure helper referenced when timer register dispatch encounters an unsupported selector.
External ordering primitive referenced by the ThunderX acknowledge path.
Alternate build variant of the external ordering primitive referenced by the same acknowledge path.
External unreachable marker referenced after timer read dispatch that cannot fall through.
External compile-time check helper referenced when validating capability constants.
External build-option query referenced when deciding capability possibility and alternative emission.
External one-time warning helper referenced when handling write-through firmware memory.
